title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Łowicz Paper Cutouts. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Łowicz Paper Cutouts
options.lineage: Wycinanki łowickie, layered Polish folk paper cutouts
options.thesis: Each person is a layered paper rosette in the Łowicz palette; everything else stays a clean phone form.
options.viewport: Emerald party strip with a scalloped edge, your rosette and greeting, a three-dot wishlist meter, the list, and Add gift in the thumb zone.
options.risk: Folk colour can tip into souvenir kitsch if it leaks past rosettes, tabs and buttons.

raised.raise: Palette discipline: only the five paper colours plus ink and paper, no stray tints.
One primary action per screen, anchored in the thumb zone.
Every section is a ruled card headed by a small coloured paper tab.
Status is a mark in a fixed cell: filled dot done, hollow dot to do.
All spacing snaps to one 4px grid.
One printed state vocabulary for done, waiting and disabled, reused on every page.

options.label: Advent Calendar Doors
options.thesis: Your draw sits behind a numbered door that opens once you have written three wishes.
options.viewport: Greeting on top, a closed door card counting down your wishes, the wishlist below and Add gift at the bottom.
options.risk: Classic red, green and gold: where most Christmas apps land.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Wishlists as strobing barcode data fields.
options.viewport: A barcode field with the draw in monospace.
options.risk: Cold and alien to a family Christmas.
options.case: Loses both axes: relatives don't identify with data art, and strobing obscures the task.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One wish per full screen, swiped through.
options.viewport: One gift fills the screen with action glyphs on the right.
options.risk: Wishlists are short text, not media, so the screens would be empty.
options.case: Loses both axes: text wishes have no media to fill the frame, and the organizer table breaks.
options.kept: One primary action in the thumb zone.

options.label: High-Density Web
options.thesis: Every party fact packed into ruled modules.
options.viewport: A dense module mosaic of people, gifts and links.
options.risk: Too small and dense for relatives on phones.
options.case: Loses both axes: tiny type fails older relatives and hides the next step.
options.kept: Ruled modules headed by a coloured tab.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: The party as a raked rack of timetable slides.
options.viewport: Raked slides listing people like departures.
options.case: Loses both axes: the travel metaphor confuses a gift exchange.
options.kept: Status as filled or hollow marks in fixed cells.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Party names built from a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: A giant grid-built party name over the list.
options.risk: Poster type eats a phone screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: designer-poster vocabulary, not family.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Wishlists set as twin columns around a key rail.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with vermilion keys between.
options.risk: Scholarly and tiny on a phone.
options.case: Loses both axes: academic tone and two columns don't fit phones.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean neutral web app with one red accent, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Header, greeting, wishlist card and a full-width red Add button.
canonCard.risk: Tidy but anonymous; nothing says family Christmas.
